Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:1.hebrew: מצאו קשור בכיס שלו או בארנקי כו' - שליח המביא גט ואבד הימנו, לאחר זמן מצאו קשור בכיס שלו או בארנקי כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:1.english: He found it tied to his pouch or to a purse, etc. - An agent bringing a bill of divorce and it was lost from him, [and] after some time he found it tied to his pouch or to a purse, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:2.english: Among his utensils - The utensils he uses in his house.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:3.hebrew: אפילו לזמן מרובה - אע"ג דתנן (גיטין דף כז.): המביא גט ואבד הימנו, מצאו לזמן מרובה פסול — הכא כשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:3.english: Even [after] a long time - Although we learned in a Mishnah (Gittin 27a): "One who brings a bill of divorce and it was lost from him, [if] he found it [after] a long time, [it is] invalid" — here [it is] valid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:4.hebrew: ניחוש לשאלה - שמא השאיל כיסו לאחר, והוא קשרו בו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:10:4.english: Let us be concerned about a loan - Perhaps he lent his pouch to someone else, and that [person] tied [the bill of divorce] to it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:11:1.hebrew: דמסמני - מנחשי, ואומר סימן לאדם שמשאיל כיסו שמוכר לו מזלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:11:1.english: That they portend - They take [it as] an omen, and one says [it is] a sign for a person who lends his pouch that he is selling his good fortune to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:11:2.hebrew: דמזייף - שהיה לכל איש חותם ניכר בטבעתו, וכששולח שום דבר סתום, מכסהו וחותמו בטבעתו. לפיכך אינו משאיל טבעתו, שמא יעשה זה חותם כנגד חותמו ויזייף בו את שליחותיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:11:2.english: That he might forge - For every person had a recognizable seal on his ring, and when he sends something closed up, he covers it and seals it with his ring. Therefore, he does not lend his ring, lest this [other person] make a seal matching his seal and forge his dispatches with it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:12:1.hebrew: אין מעידין על השומא - המעידין על האשה להשיאה, ואמרו סימן היה בו, שומא באבר פלוני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:12:1.english: One does not testify on the basis of a mole - [This refers to] those who testify concerning a woman to permit her to remarry, and said: "There was a distinguishing mark on him — a mole on such-and-such a limb."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:12:2.english: A mole - Verrue in Old French [a wart].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:12:3.hebrew: סימנין דרבנן - וגבי אשת איש, דאיסור דאורייתא הוא, לא סמכינן עלייהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:12:3.english: Distinguishing marks are by rabbinic law - And with regard to a married woman, which is a Torah prohibition, we do not rely upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:13:1.english: On one's contemporary - One who was born at the same time as him, for they were born under one constellation.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:14:1.hebrew: בסימנין העשויין כו' - אם עשויין להשתנות או אינן עשויין להשתנות. אם בחייו היתה שומא שחורה, במותו נעשית לבנה, או איפוך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:14:1.english: With regard to distinguishing marks that are apt, etc. - Whether they are apt to change or are not apt to change: if during his lifetime a mole was black, at his death it becomes white, or the reverse.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:15:1.hebrew: מובהק - ואפילו סימנין דרבנן, יש לסמוך על זה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:15:1.english: Clear-cut - And even [though regular] distinguishing marks are [only] rabbinic, one may rely on this [type of mark].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:16:1.hebrew: היכי מהדרינן - כלומר, מה תקנה ראו חכמים בדבר ליכנס בספק להחזיר ממון למי שאינו שלו: אלא ל"ג:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:16:1.english: How do we return - That is to say, what benefit did the Sages see in the matter to enter into a doubt to return money to one to whom it does not belong? We do not read [the word] "ela" ["rather"].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:17:1.hebrew: וכי אדם עושה - ובניחותא דמוצא, מאי איכפת לן אם מי שאבדה ממנו לא ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:17:1.english: But can a person perform - And [because of] the satisfaction of the finder, what do we care if the one from whom it was lost is not pleased?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:18:1.hebrew: אלא - אמר רבא: כל אובדי אבידה ניחא להו שתהא דת זו בישראל למיתב סימנין, וכל הבא ונותנו יטלנה. מאי טעמא? מידע ידע דעדים לית ליה - פעמים שאין לו עדים עליה, ואם יזקיקוהו לעדים לא תבא לעולם לידו. ומימר אמר: טוב לי שיחזירוה לכל האומר סימניה, דלא שכיחא דנימא סימנין דידה אלא אנא, דכ"ע לא ידעי כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:18:1.english: Rather - Rava said: All who lose a lost item are pleased that this law should be [practiced] in Israel, to give distinguishing marks, and whoever comes and gives [them] shall take it. What is the reason? He knows that he has no witnesses — sometimes he has no witnesses for it, and if they require witnesses of him, it will never come into his hand. And he says [to himself]: It is better for me that they return it to anyone who states its distinguishing marks, for it is uncommon that anyone should state its distinguishing marks other than me, since no one knows [them], etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:19:1.hebrew: אלא הא דתנן כו' - ואמרו להחזיר לו למלוה בלא עדים, בסימן זה שאומר: שלשה היו ומשלשה לוים. ואם מן הלוה נפלו, שכבר פרעם, מי ניחא ליה בתקנה זו שיתנם המוצאם לכל הבא ונותן סימניהם? והלא טוב לו שיהו מונחים ביד המוצאם עולמית? דכל זמן שהם בידו ולא יחזירם למלוה, הרי הם כשרופים! ולא ניחא דליהדר להו בסימנין, דלמא מיתרמי דידע מלוה בסימניהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:19:1.english: But [there is] that which we learned, etc. - And they said to return [the documents] to him, to the creditor, without witnesses, by this distinguishing mark that he says, "There were three [notes], and [they were] from three debtors." And if they fell from the debtor, who had already paid them, is he satisfied with this enactment that the one who finds them should give them to anyone who comes and provides their distinguishing marks? Is it not better for him that they remain in the finder's possession forever? For as long as they are in his possession and he does not return them to the creditor, they are as if burned! And [thus] it is not satisfactory [to the debtor] that he should return them by distinguishing marks, lest it happen that the creditor knows their distinguishing marks.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:1:1.english: To return a bill of divorce - That was lost by the agent bringing it before he gave [it] to her.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:1:2.english: An ordinance - Later in our sugya, [the Gemara] explains what it is.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:1:3.english: With regard to monetary matters - For [property] declared ownerless by the court is ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:20:1.hebrew: התם - בסימנין כי האי, לא איכפת לן בניחותא דלוה, דודאי לאו מיניה נפיל, דהנך שטרי אחריני מאי בעו גביה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:20:1.english: There - With distinguishing marks like this, we are not concerned about the debtor's interest, for [the document] certainly did not fall from him, as what would those other documents be doing with him?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:2:1.hebrew: תובעין אצטריכא ליה - קרא לתובעין אתא, ולמעוטי מידי דאיאוש ואפקריה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:2:1.english: [The mention of] claimants was necessary for him - The verse came [to teach the requirement of] claimants, and to exclude something that [the owner] despaired of and declared ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:2:2.hebrew: כדי נסבה - בלא מקרא, אלא אסמכינהו אקרא בעלמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:2:2.english: [He] cited it for no reason - Without a [Scriptural] verse; rather, [he] merely supported them on a verse.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:3:1.hebrew: ת"ש - דאוקמינן לעיל, חמור לסימני אוכף אתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:3:1.english: Come and hear - For we established earlier [that] "donkey" comes for [the] distinguishing marks of [the] saddle.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:3:2.hebrew: אימא בעדי אוכף - אם יש עדים המכירין בטביעות עין לאוכף שהוא שלו, מחזירין לו את החמור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:3:2.english: Say: On the basis of witnesses of the saddle - If there are witnesses who recognize by visual recognition that the saddle is his, we return the donkey to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:4:1.hebrew: דרשהו - והכי משמע: "עד דרוש אחיך אותו" — עד דרשך את אחיך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:4:1.english: Scrutinize him - And this is what [the verse] means: "until your brother claims it" [ad derosh achikha oto] — until you scrutinize your brother.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:5:1.english: With witnesses - That he should bring witnesses that it is his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:6:1.hebrew: אין מעידין - על אדם שמת להשיא את אשתו, אלא אם כן ראו פרצוף פניו שהוא עם החוטם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:6:1.english: One does not testify - regarding a man who died, to permit his wife to remarry, unless they saw the countenance of his face, which is with the nose.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:7:1.hebrew: דארוך או גוץ - שאין זה סימן, שהרבה ארוכין וגוצים יש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:7:1.english: That [he was] tall or short - For this is not a distinguishing mark, as there are many tall and short [people].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:7:3.hebrew: חיישינן - שמא השאילם לאחר, ואותו אחר ראו שמת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:7:3.english: We are concerned - Perhaps he lent them to another [person], and [it was] that other [person] whom they saw had died.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:8:1.english: [It] wounds - Doroissier in Old French [meaning to chafe or injure the back].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:9:1.hebrew: חיורי או סומקי - אין זה סימן, שהרבה כאלה יש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27b:9:1.english: White or red - This is not a distinguishing mark, for there are many like these.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:10:1.hebrew: מצאו - גט קשור בכיס, יחזיר המוצא לשליח או לבעל השואלו בסימני הכיס:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:10:1.english: If he found it - [If one found] a bill of divorce tied to a pouch, the finder returns [it] to the agent or to the husband who asks for it by the distinguishing marks of the pouch:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:10:2.hebrew: (וניחוש לשאלה) - וא"ת: ולוכח מהכא דסימנין דאורייתא, ובפרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קכ. ושם ד"ה מצאו) פריך מהכא דסימנין דאורייתא. וי"ל: דמצי לאוקמה כגון שאותו שאבדו מצאו, ומכיר הכיס בטביעות עין, דכיון שבעצמו מצאו — נאמן. וה"נ הוה מצי למדחי התם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:10:2.english: (And let us be concerned about a loan) - And if you ask: Why not prove from here that distinguishing marks are [effective by] biblical law — and indeed in the last chapter of Yevamot (120a, there, s.v. metza'o) [the Gemara] challenges from here that distinguishing marks are [effective by] biblical law? One can answer that [the Gemara] could have established [the baraita] in a case where the very person who lost it found it, and he recognizes the pouch by visual recognition [tevi'ut ayin]; for since he himself found it, he is believed. And so too [the Gemara] could have deflected [the challenge] there.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:11:1.hebrew: כיס וארנקי משום דמסמני - וא"ת: והכתיב "לא תנחשו"? וי"ל: בשלהי במה אשה (שבת דף סז.) אמרינן, כל דבר שיש בו משום רפואה — אין בו משום דרכי האמורי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:11:1.english: A pouch and a purse, due to [the fact] that they portend [bad fortune] - And if you will say: But is it not written, "You shall not practice divination"? And one can say [in answer]: At the end of [the chapter] Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 67a), we say: Anything that has [a purpose] of healing in it does not constitute [a violation of] the ways of the Amorites.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:18:1.hebrew: ואנא יהיבנא סימנים מובהקין דידה - לא מובהקין ממש קאמר, אלא מובהקים מסימני חבירו, כמו: "זה אומר מדת ארכו וזה אומר מדת רחבו". ולקמן (בבא מציעא דף כח:) נמי דקאמר: "לעולם גלימא מכריז, ולא אמר סימנין מובהקין", התם נמי לאו מובהקים ממש קאמר, אלא שלא אמר סימנים טובים שיש בו, כי אם כסימנין דסומקי וחיורי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:18:1.english: "And I will provide its clear-cut distinguishing marks" - [The Gemara] does not mean literally conclusive [distinguishing marks], rather [marks that are] more distinctive than those of his fellow, such as: "One states the measure of its length and the other states the measure of its width." And below (Bava Metzia 28b) as well, where [the Gemara] says: "Actually, he announces [that he found] a cloak, and [the claimant] did not state clear-cut distinguishing marks," there too it does not mean literally conclusive [marks], rather that he did not state the good distinguishing marks that are on it, [having stated] only [marks] like signs of red and white:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:3:1.hebrew: ת"ש חמור בסימני אוכף - ברייתא היא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:3:1.english: Come and hear: a donkey on the basis of the distinguishing marks of the saddle - [This] is a baraita:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:4:1.hebrew: דרשהו אם הוא רמאי מאי לאו בסימנין - וא"ת, דבמתני' (לקמן בבא מציעא כח:) דריש מהאי קרא דלא יחזיר אף בסימנין? וי"ל, דאסמכתא היא, כדקתני עלה בברייתא: "משרבו הרמאים התקינו", אבל הכא משמע ליה שהיא דרשה גמורה, מדקאמר "וכי תעלה על דעתך לומר" כו'. ועי"ל, דבמתני' מיירי בידוע שהוא רמאי, לכך צריך עדים, אבל הכא מיירי בסתם בני אדם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27b:4:1.english: "Scrutinize him whether he is a swindler ... is it not with distinguishing marks?" - And if you ask: In the Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 28b), it expounds from this verse that one may not return [a lost item] even with distinguishing marks? One can answer that [the exposition in the Mishnah] is an asmakhta [a scriptural support for a rabbinic enactment], as it is taught regarding it in a baraita: "When swindlers multiplied, they instituted [this]"; whereas here it seems to [the Gemara] that it is a full-fledged exposition, since it says: "Would it enter your mind to say, etc." And one can further answer that the Mishnah is speaking of one who is known to be a swindler — therefore he requires witnesses — whereas here [the Gemara] is speaking of ordinary people.
